sample_unit: patients tested for AHP in diagnosis cohort (72 cases, 347 negatives); referral cohort 100,596 patients
models_evaluated: diagnosis model (machine learning, range of architectures)

links.outcome: Model performance on local historical data, plus prospective biochemical testing of flagged current patients
links.effect: Best referral models F-score 86-91%; diagnosis model F-score 92%. Of 372 flagged patients only 10 recruited for testing, all negative; post hoc, 71% of cases identified earlier, saving 1.2 years.
links.quote: However, we were only able to recruit 10 of these patients for biochemical testing, all of whom were negative.

unlisted_practices: Using knowledge-graph data for semi-automated feature selection in rare disease prediction models
Two-stage referral and diagnosis models to flag undiagnosed rare disease patients

screen.reason: The study develops and tests ML models to identify patients with undiagnosed acute hepatic porphyria, including a prospective outreach/screening deployment where 372 predicted patients were contacted for testing, but it does not compare or evaluate a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
